title: AI Note-Taking Tools That Actually Save You Time
hook: You are probably forgetting half of every meeting you attend.

narration.text: You are probably forgetting half of every meeting you attend. AI note-taking tools are changing that, and a few of them are genuinely impressive.
Otter.ai has been around for a while and it remains one of the most reliable options. It transcribes your conversations in real time and lets you search through the text afterwards.
Fireflies.ai goes a step further by joining your video calls automatically. It produces a summary, pulls out action items, and lets your whole team access the notes in one place.
Notion AI sits inside a tool many people already use for notes and documents. It can summarise, rewrite, and help you organise anything you throw at it.
Microsoft OneNote now has Copilot built in, so if your organisation already runs on Microsoft 365, you may already have access to AI-assisted note features without paying extra.
Mem is worth a look if you want something built around AI from the ground up. It automatically links related notes together, so your ideas connect without you having to organise them manually.
The honest truth is that none of these tools are perfect. They work best when you pick one that fits how you already work, rather than forcing a new habit.
Which of these tools have you tried, and did it actually stick? Drop your answer in the comments, and follow the channel for a daily look at AI tools worth knowing about.

description: AI note-taking tools promise to save you time, but not all of them deliver. This video breaks down the options that are genuinely useful, from real-time transcription to automatic meeting summaries. Find the one that fits your workflow and stop losing track of important information.
